QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_16

question.text: Which of the following AIF types is exempted from the requirement of annual audit of PPM terms, WITHOUT needing any specific waiver from investors?

answer.text: Category I SME AIFs with corpus below ₹100 crore.
Angel Funds whose total investments at cost exceed ₹100 crore.
Large Value Funds (LVFs) as defined in SEBI (AIF) Regulations.

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter lists three exemption categories. Among them, Large Value Funds (LVFs) are exempt WITHOUT needing any specific investor waiver. Other exemption — AIFs/schemes where each investor commits at least ₹70 crore (USD 10 million) — requires a specific investor WAIVER. Angel Funds with investments above ₹100 crore are, from FY 2025-26 onwards, mandatorily REQUIRED to audit — opposite of exemption. The Trap: Corpus-below-100cr SME and Cat II Infra are not specific exemptions under the PPM-audit framework. Angel Funds >₹100cr is the exact reverse — they now must audit (FY 2025-26 onward). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C also tests the LVF no-waiver exemption. The 'LVF' concept (commitment from Accredited Investors) was introduced via the June 2022 circular. Manager's Pro-Tip: For LVF structures, even though PPM audit is not mandated, still commission a voluntary annual PPM-compliance certificate — future LPs in successor funds will ask for it during diligence.
